targets.title: The development of regulatory functions from birth to 5 years: Insights from premature infants.
targets.evidence_quote: This analytic step was a confirmatory effort to replicate Feldman's (2009) findings, on top of which we included the estimation of stability paths over time to provide more robust findings.
targets.outcome_quote: Our first hypothesis was to replicate Feldman's (2009) model that established the developmental pathway of physiological regulation before age 1 → emotion regulation before age 1 → attention regulation between age 1-2 → self-regulation at age 5. In contrast, our study identified three major pathways: attention regulation at 6 months predicted physiological regulation at 15 months, attention regulation at 15 months predicted emotion regulation at 24 months, and attention regulation at 24 months predicted better self-regulation (greater executive functions, compliance, and fewer behavioral problems) in preschool age. Our findings are consistent with Feldman's (2009) study in several ways. First, both the current study and Feldman's (2009) study support the conceptualization that the development of self-regulation is an ongoing process during early childhood.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors identify both agreement and explicitly contrasting pathways. Their opening statement that the study replicated the earlier study describes the undertaking; favorable evidence for the model is not an unqualified overall replication verdict. Explicit differences in sequential pathways and support for attention regulation make the aggregated outcome mixed.
